Track pay-per-use credit spend and set spending-limit/auto-recharge behavior

approval.cost: Pay-per-usage API pricing (no subscriptions): Posts Read $0.005; User Read $0.010; DM Event Read $0.010; Following/Followers Read $0.010; List/Space/Community/Note Read $0.005; Like/Mute/Block Read $0.001; Owned Reads $0.001 per resource; Post Create $0.015; Post Create (with URL) $0.200; Post Create (summoned) $0.010; DM Interaction Create $0.015; User Interaction Create $0.015; Interaction Delete $0.010. 'All resources are deduplicated within a 24-hour UTC day window.' Spending controls: 'Set a maximum amount you can spend per billing cycle... When the limit is reached, API requests will be blocked until the next billing cycle.' xAI credit kickback on cumulative per-cycle spend: $0-$199 0%; $200-$499 10%; $500-$999 15%; $1,000+ 20% back in free xAI API credits. Enterprise API pricing was not stated on the pages read
approval.trigger: No per-app OAuth review is described in the docs for the standard X API: developer sign-up and app creation are self-serve, and end users can authorize your app as soon as it is configured. There is no pre-approval user/install cap documented for user-context OAuth. Exceptions that DO require a request/approval: the Ads API ('You will need to request access and be approved for Ads API access. Use the Ads API Access Form to submit a request for each of your developer app(s)'), Enterprise API access (interest form / sales process), and specific products with their own access forms (e.g. Livestream API). App suspension exists as an enforcement path: 'If your app shows as suspended, check your email for a notice from the X platform team. Use the Platform Help Form to appeal.'
approval.wait: None for the standard API (no approval duration is stated for developer accounts or for the Ads API/Enterprise requests)

blockers.detail: 'The auth_code has a time limit of 30 seconds once the App owner receives an approved auth_code from the user. You will have to exchange it with an access token within 30 seconds, or the auth_code will expire.'
blockers.howToClear: Exchange the code synchronously in the callback handler; never queue it.
blockers.title: The 30-second authorization code

blockers.detail: 'By default, the access token you create through the Authorization Code Flow with PKCE will only stay valid for two hours unless you've used the offline.access scope', and if the scope is not passed, 'we will not generate a refresh token', forcing re-authorization every two hours.
blockers.howToClear: Always request offline.access for any durable connection.
blockers.title: No offline.access, no refresh token, and a 2-hour connection

blockers.detail: Because access is credit-based, a depleted balance or a hit spending limit blocks API calls mid-flight. The docs describe auto-recharge safeguards (at most one top-up per 5-minute window; auto-recharge paused at zero/negative balance).
blockers.howToClear: Purchase credits upfront, set auto-recharge, and monitor spend per billing cycle.
blockers.title: Billing is a runtime dependency

alternatives: OAuth 1.0a User Context (legacy 3-legged flow; permissions are coarse and set once at the App level: Read only / Read and write / Read, write, and DMs; every request individually signed HMAC-SHA1; still required or accepted by some v1.1-era endpoints, but some v2 endpoints reject it entirely, e.g. bookmarks: 'OAuth 1.0a User Context is forbidden for this endpoint')

OAuth 2.0 App-Only / Bearer Token ('authenticates requests on behalf of your developer App... typically for developers that need read-only access to public information'; cannot act on behalf of a user)
OAuth 1.0a token exchange grant ('Apps with existing OAuth 1.0a users can also use the token exchange grant to convert stored OAuth 1.0a access tokens into OAuth 2.0 tokens')
PIN-based OAuth (OAuth 1.0a, for apps that cannot open a browser or receive a callback)
flavor.recommended: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow with PKCE (OAuth 2.0 User Context) on an App in the X Developer Console
flavor.why: The object is an App in the X Developer Console (console.x.com): 'a container for your API credentials. Each app has its own keys, tokens, and settings.' Creating an App can generate four credential sets: API Key & Secret (identify your app; sign OAuth 1.0a requests), Bearer Token (app-only auth for public data), Access Token & Secret (your own account, OAuth 1.0a), and Client ID & Secret (OAuth 2.0 user-context). An App's authentication settings can be OAuth 1.0a, OAuth 2.0, or both; 'OAuth 2.0 can be used with the X API v2 only.' The 2.0 flow 'allows you to authenticate on behalf of another user with more control over an application's scopes', with a consent screen showing only the requested scopes. App type determines the client class: Web App and Automated App/Bot are confidential (receive a Client Secret); Native App and Single Page App are public ('Public clients use PKCE only'). Scope catalog includes tweet.read/write, users.read, users.email, follows.read/write, offline.access ('Stay connected to your account until you revoke access'), like/list/block/mute read+write, dm.read/write, media.write, and more.

humanMust: Sign up for a developer account at console.x.com and accept the Developer Agreement / Developer Policy
Create the App and configure User authentication settings (app type, Callback URLs, Website URL)
Save the credentials from Keys and Tokens (Client ID, and Client Secret for confidential clients)
Set up billing for pay-per-use: purchase credits, optionally set a spending limit and auto-recharge
name: X (Twitter)
nuances: PKCE is structural, not optional: the supported grant types for user authorization are 'authorization code with PKCE and refresh token'. Token requests from public clients must carry client_id in the body; confidential clients authenticate with an HTTP Basic header (base64 of Client ID : Client Secret).

Callback rules: URLs must be on the app's allowlist and 'must match exactly (including trailing slashes)'; maximum 10 callback URLs per app; use https in production; for local development use http://127.0.0.1 (not localhost); javascript, data, file, ftp, mailto, telnet schemes are disallowed. OAuth 2.0 uses exact-match validation. The state parameter may be up to 500 characters.

OAuth 1.0a contrast: user tokens 'do not expire but can be revoked by the user at any time', and with GET oauth/authorize 'the user will always be prompted to authorize access to your application, even if access was previously granted'. Revocation for 2.0: POST oauth2/revoke ('used to enable a log out feature in clients'); users can also revoke from X's connected Apps page.

Rate-limit note: limits are mostly the same as OAuth 1.0a, 'with the exception of Tweets lookup and Users lookup. We are increasing the per-App limit from 300 to 900 requests per 15 minutes while using OAuth 2.0.' Bot apps can link a managing account (Settings > Your account > Automation) to label the account as automated.

The pay-per-use model replaced subscriptions in the current docs: 'The X API uses pay-per-usage pricing. No subscriptions, pay only for what you use.' The changelog describes its origin as 'a limited closed pilot for a new credit-based, usage-based pricing model... no fixed subscription fees and no monthly object caps.' A separate Enterprise API documentation tree exists with its own getting-access and pricing pages and an Enterprise interest form.
prerequisites: A developer account at console.x.com (Developer Agreement / Developer Policy accepted)
Callback URL(s) and Website URL for the App (exact-match rules)
Prepaid API credits for pay-per-use access

steps.detail: 'Get started with the X API in three steps: sign up, create an app, and save your credentials.' Create the App in the Developer Console.
steps.title: Sign up; create an App

steps.detail: Choose the Type of App (Web App / Automated App or Bot = confidential; Native App / Single Page App = public), add Callback URL(s) (max 10, exact match including trailing slashes) and Website URL, and set the OAuth 1.0a permission level if you will use it. Save the credentials from Keys and Tokens.
steps.title: Configure User authentication settings; save credentials

steps.detail: Purchase credits in the Developer Console; optionally set a per-billing-cycle spending limit and auto-recharge. 'Purchase credits upfront. Deducted as you use the API.'
steps.title: Set up pay-per-use billing

steps.detail: GET x.com/i/oauth2/authorize with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, scope (space-separated, including offline.access), state (random CSRF string, up to 500 characters), code_challenge, and code_challenge_method (S256 or plain). The user authenticates and approves or declines.
steps.title: Build the authorize URL (PKCE + offline.access)

steps.detail: The code expires in 30 seconds. POST api.x.com/2/oauth2/token (form-encoded) with code, grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, redirect_uri, code_verifier (plus the Basic-auth header for confidential clients). The response includes a refresh token only if offline.access was requested. Call X API v2 endpoints with the access token as a Bearer token.
steps.title: Exchange the code within 30 seconds

steps.detail: POST api.x.com/2/oauth2/token with grant_type=refresh_token, refresh_token, client_id (Basic header for confidential clients). Revoke on disconnect via POST oauth2/revoke with the token and client_id.
steps.title: Refresh; revoke on disconnect

tagline: Self-serve OAuth 2.0 with PKCE and no app review, but the sharpest code lifetime in the library (30 seconds), a 2-hour access token unless you request offline.access, and an API that is now billed per call with prepaid credits.

time.active: ~25 min of console and billing setup + ~1-2 hrs of flow code
time.total: Same day; no approval wait for the standard API
time.waiting: None for standard OAuth (Ads API and Enterprise access are form-gated, durations not stated)
